expl.summary: Each jet (its 8 hardest particles) is placed on 16 neurons, each a clipped sum of if-statements on jet observables, and each of the five class scores adds some neurons and subtracts others. This formula (336 terms) is the one-term version of formula 399: each observable appears in at most one term per neuron, re-tuned on the network's predictions; it classifies 65.0% of validation jets correctly. The t score is built mainly on spread: it subtracts neuron 13 (ΣzΔR below 0.148 and λ₁ below 0.0161; tops average 1.20 on it, the other classes 4.16-5.24; -49%) and adds neuron 10 (λ₁ above 0.00417, τ₁ above 0.057; +28%), so it follows ΣzΔR and λ₁+λ₂ with rank correlations of 0.915 and 0.913. The q score is mostly neuron 9 (ΣzΔR² below 0.00365, centred pT; +55%) minus neuron 10 (-21%), and falls with mass and max m_pair(3 subjets) (rank correlations -0.74 and -0.73). The g score also adds neuron 9 (+23%), and in addition neuron 2 (rises with pT₇, small Σz(ΔR/0.8)^½ and m/ΣpT; +36%, its largest input) and neuron 1 (ΣzΔR above 0.0991, ln ΣpT above 6.54; +14%); it subtracts neuron 5 (z₇ below 0.0522, pT held by the hardest particles; -14%), which is largest for quarks; it rises with z₇ (rank correlation 0.574). The two boson scores share neuron 7 (m/ΣpT at most 0.0909 with mass above 64.5 GeV; +12% of W, +33% of Z) and neuron 13 (+8% of each), and subtract neuron 3 (ΣzΔR above 0.0267, subjet axes far apart: -16% of W, -25% of Z) and neuron 6 (-8.2% and -13%). They are split by the W score adding neuron 11 (λ₁+λ₂ below 0.00872; +22%) and neuron 0 (ΣzΔR² below 0.013, mass above 53.2 GeV; +10%), which the Z score does not use, and subtracting neurons 15 (-9.1%) and 14 (-9%), while the Z score adds neuron 14 (+6%). One offered particle-mass threshold is used: mass > 91.2 GeV (the Z mass) in neuron 12, which does not enter any class score; since the mass here is that of the 8 particles seen, it acts as an ordinary cut on large mass.
